  - [wrong] A-Q — Compare the side cards. A-Q beats your pair of aces with its higher side card.
    BETTER ANSWER: A-T
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Jd | Board Ah 7c 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Seat focus btn, bb | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Flop | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  + [correct] A-T — Your jack beats the ten. A-T can call with a weaker pair of aces. Your jack is higher than its ten.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Jd | Board Ah 7c 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Seat focus btn, bb | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Flop | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] A-J — Same best five. A-J ties your A-J on A-7-2. A call from the same hand splits the pot; the value target is the weaker A-T.
    BETTER ANSWER: A-T
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Jd | Board Ah 7c 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Seat focus btn, bb | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Flop | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

TASK w4_checkpoint_price [drill] Call or fold
CAPTION: HJ bet 3 BB on the turn. Compare your chance to win with the call divided by the pot after you call.
Q: 6-max micro-stakes model. Two players, no ties or more bets. If you call, you win 1 time in 4 (25%). Which earns more, call or fold?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Compare the stated chance with the share of the final pot you pay.
TABLE: Turn | You 8s 7d | Board Kh 8c 4d 2s | Pot 10 BB | To call 3 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1 | Center Turn decision | Facts one pair, middle pair
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ stack 94.25 BB bet 3 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer 8s 7d stack 97.25 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB folded stack 99 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ raises 2.75 BB · CO folds · BTN calls 2.75 BB · SB folds · BB folds · Flop: HJ checks · BTN checks · Turn: HJ bets 3 BB
  + [correct] Call [3 BB] — Compare the two chances. 3 ÷ (3 + 10) is about 23%. You win 1 time in 4, or 25%, so the call earns more.
  - [wrong] Fold — Find the threshold from the displayed price. You need about a 23% chance at this price. One win in four is enough, so folding gives up a profitable call.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call
  - [suboptimal] Call because 25% wins often enough — The action fits. Compare the price too. You must pay 3 BB for a 13 BB final pot. At about 23% to break even, 25% just covers it. On a bigger wager that same win rate can lose chips.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call

  - [wrong] Fold — Compare with the break-even chance. Folding gives up a profitable call in this model: 30% is higher than the roughly 22.2% you need.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON board_texture_basics · Dry or wet board =====

TASK board_texture_basics_w5_texture_intro [theory] Board texture
CAPTION: Board texture asks how much the next cards can change.
TEACH: What can change? A dry board has few ways for the next card to change who leads. A wet board has many. When ranks sit close together or suits match, more hands can improve.
TEACH LABELS: Rank gaps, Suits
Q: What does board texture describe?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Dry boards change less. Wet boards create more threats.
TABLE: Flop | You Ac Jd | Board Ks 8h 3c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat HJ | Active hj | Decision hj | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Read the flop | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ Ac Jd stack 97.5 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ raises 2.5 BB · CO folds · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Rank gaps and matching suits tell you how much the next card can change.

TASK board_texture_basics_w5_dry_board [drill] Two ways a flop can change
CAPTION: Read the three flop cards.
Q: What texture is this?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Few obvious straight or flush paths are visible.
TABLE: Flop | You Ah Tc | Board Kc 7d 2s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Read the flop | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Ah Tc stack 97.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
  + [correct] Dry — Sharp read. Spread ranks and mixed suits make this a dry board.
  - [wrong] Wet — Not quite. K-7-2 has three suits and wide gaps. Treating it as wet can make you pay to protect against unlikely straights and flushes.
    BETTER ANSWER: Dry
  - [wrong] Semi-wet — The flop has few short paths. K-7-2 has wide rank gaps and three suits. Marking it semi-wet gives too much weight to hands that still need both remaining cards.
    BETTER ANSWER: Dry

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON connected_boards · Connected boards =====

TASK connected_boards_w5_connected_intro [theory] Connected ranks
CAPTION: Connected ranks sit close together, like 9-8-7.
TEACH: Ranks can connect. Check the gap on each side of the middle rank. On 9-8-7, a player holding J-T can use every flop rank to make a straight. That possibility exists before anyone bets. With Q-J instead, you still need a ten to make five consecutive ranks.
TEACH LABELS: 9, 8, 7, Connected
TEACH: Ranks and suits describe different things. A paired board repeats one of its ranks. Two-tone means two flop cards share a suit. A draw is a hand that needs another card to complete.
TEACH TABLE: Flop | You Qd Jc | Board 9c 9h 4c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Facts one pair, two-tone, paired board, backdoor flush, backdoor straight
TEACH TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
Q: What makes a board connected?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Close ranks create more straight paths.
TABLE: Flop | You Qd Jc | Board 9h 8s 7d | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Read the ranks | Facts high card, rainbow, consecutive board, gutshot, completion cards 4
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Qd Jc stack 97.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Three nearby ranks, such as 9-8-7, give private cards more ways to complete a straight.

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON flush_draws · Flush draws =====

TASK flush_draws_w5_flush_intro [theory] Same suit pressure
CAPTION: A flush draw appears when one more suit card can help.
TEACH: Four cards of the same suit. A flush draw has four cards of one suit between your hand and the board. There are 13 cards in a suit, so 13 minus 4 leaves 9 that can complete your flush.
TEACH LABELS: Suit, Heart, Flush draw
TEACH: Allow for both remaining cards. Rainbow means the three flop cards have different suits. A backdoor draw needs both the turn and the river to help.
Q: What does a flush draw need?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Count suits on the board and in hand.
TABLE: Flop | You Kh Jh | Board Qh 8h 3s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat HJ | Active hj | Decision hj | Center Count matching suits | Facts high card, two-tone, flush draw, backdoor straight, completion cards 9
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ Kh Jh stack 97.5 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ raises 2.5 BB · CO folds · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Four cards of one suit leave you one card short of a flush.

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON straight_draws · Straight draws =====

TASK straight_draws_w5_straight_intro [theory] Rank ladder
CAPTION: A straight draw uses nearby ranks to chase a five-card line.
TEACH: Count the ranks that finish a straight. An open-ended draw can finish at either end of four ranks in a row. Here, 8-9-T-J can be finished by any 7 or queen: 8 outs. A gutshot has one gap, like 5-6-8-9. Only a 7 fills it: 4 outs.
TEACH LABELS: Ranks, Ladder, Straight draw
Q: What does a straight draw use?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Look for rank ladders.

TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Check which next rank could give you five consecutive cards.

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON outs_improvement · Outs as improvement cards =====

TASK outs_improvement_w5_outs_intro [theory] Improvement cards
CAPTION: Outs are cards that can improve your hand.
TEACH: Count the cards that help. An out is an unseen card that improves your hand. With one card left and 46 unseen, 9 outs hit about 1 time in 5, 8 about 1 in 6, and 4 about 1 in 12.
TEACH LABELS: Outs, One card left
TEACH: Compare with the price from World 4. A 1 BB call into a 7 BB pot needs 1 win in 8. If only those 8 outs win and there are no more bets, about 1 win in 6 beats that price.
TEACH LABELS: Call 1 BB, Pot 7 BB, Chance to win
Q: What is an out?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Count the cards that complete the draw. Then compare the chance with the price.

TASK outs_improvement_w5_clean_vs_risky_out_transfer [drill] Safer out or risky out
CAPTION: Real table. Turn board shows A-heart, 7-heart, 6-club, 2-diamond. You have 9-spade and 8-diamond.
TEACH: Not every helping card is equally clean. A card can improve your hand and still make the board more dangerous. Start with simple language: safer out when the board stays calmer, riskier out when the board adds new danger.

===== WORLD 5 · LESSON turn_river_changes · Turn and river changes =====

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_bucket_basics · Range buckets =====

TASK w6_range_intro [theory] Three buckets
CAPTION: A range is the group of hands that fit a situation.
TEACH: Three buckets. After the flop, sort your hand into value (can bet for profit), bluff candidate (can make better hands fold), or missed (check or fold).
TEACH LABELS: Hand strength, Can it improve?, What folds?
Q: What are range buckets?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Value, bluff candidate, and missed are the three range buckets.
TABLE: Flop | You Ad Js | Board Jh 8c 3d | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Center Read the flop | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Ad Js stack 97.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: A range collects the hands that fit a situation. Read the flop before placing a hand in a bucket.

TASK w6_value_dry_board [drill] Value on dry board
CAPTION: K-7-2 rainbow. You hold K-Q.
TEACH: Dry-board range buckets. After the flop, sort your hand into value (weaker hands can call), bluff candidate (better hands can fold), or missed (usually check or fold).
TEACH LABELS: Hand strength, Can it improve?, What folds?
Q: What can KQ do if weaker kings will call a small bet?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Top pair with a good kicker.
TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kc 7d 2s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Center Range bucket? | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Kd Qc stack 97.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
  + [correct] Bet for value — Top pair can bet for value. KQ pairs the highest card on K-7-2. A weaker king can call a small bet.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kc 7d 2s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] Bet as a bluff — Think about calls from weaker hands. KQ makes top pair on K-7-2. Treating the bet as a bluff misses why you want a weaker king to call.
    BETTER ANSWER: Bet for value
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kc 7d 2s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] Check because you missed — The king makes a pair. KQ shares a king with K-7-2. Treating it as a miss can give up a call from a weaker king.
    BETTER ANSWER: Bet for value
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kc 7d 2s | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

TASK w6_missed_dry_board [drill] Missed on dry board
CAPTION: BB checks with a pair, Q-J, or A-9. BB calls a half-pot bet with any pair and folds Q-J and A-9. In this example, check if you can already beat either unpaired hand.
TEACH: Compare the three buckets. Before acting postflop, sort your hand into value, bluff candidate, or missed by asking what calls and what folds.
TEACH LABELS: Hand strength, Can it improve?, What folds?
Q: What do you do with ace-queen after BB checks?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Compare the high cards if neither hand improves.
TABLE: Flop | You As Qd | Board Kh 7s 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Center Range bucket? | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight

TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO folds · BTN raises 2.5 BB · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
  + [correct] Check — Ace-high can win. A-Q missed the flop, but if nobody improves, it beats both Q-J and A-9. The rule says to check when your hand can already win.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Qd | Board Kh 7s 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
  - [suboptimal] Bet half pot as a bluff — Ace-high has a reason to check. A bet makes Q-J and A-9 fold. A-Q is already ahead of both, so that is not the goal in this example.
    BETTER ANSWER: Check
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Qd | Board Kh 7s 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
  - [wrong] Bet half pot for value — The weaker hands would fold. A-Q has no pair here. Both weaker high-card hands fold under the rule, so they cannot pay off a value bet.
    BETTER ANSWER: Check
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You As Qd | Board Kh 7s 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Card focus hero_0, hero_1, board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Range bucket? | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_board_fit · Range meets board =====

TASK w6_board_fit_intro [theory] Board shifts bucket
CAPTION: Board texture can shift a hand from value to missed.
TEACH: Board changes the bucket. A preflop strong hand can become missed if it does not connect with the flop. An overpair is a pocket pair higher than every rank on the flop.
TEACH LABELS: Board fit, Value, Missed, Texture
TEACH: Compare both ranges. Range advantage is about which player has more strong hands on this board. In this lesson, use only the hands listed for each player and count hand types that make two pair or better.
TEACH LABELS: Preflop raiser, Caller, Two pair or better

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_pressure_lines · Value, bluff, missed =====

TASK w6_pressure_lines_intro [theory] Bucket shapes action
CAPTION: Each range bucket suggests a different action direction.
TEACH: Bucket shapes action. Value bets can be paid by worse hands. Fold equity comes from the chance an opponent folds to your bet. Missed hands usually check or fold.
TEACH LABELS: Bet value, Bluff, Check-fold
Q: What does a value hand do?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Value bets to get called. Bluff candidates can bet to fold out better hands.
TABLE: Flop | You Ac Qd | Board Qh 8s 3d | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Center Read the flop | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Ac Qd stack 97.5 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.5 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Before betting, decide whether you want a weaker hand to call or a better hand to fold.

TASK w6_value_range_action [drill] Value bets
CAPTION: BB checks, then calls half-pot bets with weaker pairs such as K-J and 7-6.
Q: What is the purpose of a half-pot bet here?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Think about which hands would pay to see the turn.
TABLE: Flop | You Kh Qs | Board Kd 7s 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Center After BB checks | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

  - [wrong] Check — A check gives a free card. Checking is legal. The question asks what a half-pot bet does under the stated rule. It can get a call from a weaker pair.
    BETTER ANSWER: Bet for value
  - [wrong] Bet as a bluff — The bet earns a call. BB can call with a weaker pair, such as K-J or 7-6. You are betting to get called by worse hands.
    BETTER ANSWER: Bet for value
  + [correct] Bet for value — Weaker pairs can pay. BB can call this half-pot bet with weaker pairs such as K-J or 7-6. That gives the bet a value purpose. Comparing bet with check requires knowing how often BB calls or raises with each hand.

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_combo_counts · Count the combos =====

TASK w6_combo_counts_intro [theory] Why combo counts matter
CAPTION: Ranges are not just hand names. They also have combo counts.
TEACH: Families have counts. A combo is one exact two-card hand. Four aces times four kings gives 16 A-K combos. Four share a suit and 12 do not. A pocket pair has six ways to choose two of its four cards.
TEACH LABELS: 16 combos, 6 combos, Range density
Q: Why do combo counts matter?
HINT [theoryOnly]: First count the possible hands. To weigh a range, ask how often each one takes the action.
TABLE: Preflop | You Jc 9d | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG Jc 9d stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
REVIEW: A hand family represents several different two-card combinations. Count them to see how much weight each family has.

TASK w6_ak_combos [drill] AK combo count
CAPTION: A-K can be suited or offsuit.
TEACH: Count the cards of each rank. For two different ranks, each available card of the first rank can pair with each available card of the second rank.
TEACH LABELS: Available cards, Two ranks, Pair the cards
Q: How many combos does A-K have before blockers?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Four aces can pair with four kings. A blocker is a visible or known card that removes possible private-card combinations.
TABLE: Preflop | You Tc 9h | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG Tc 9h stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
  - [wrong] 12 combos — Not quite. 12 counts only the offsuit versions. Add the 4 suited combos and A-K reaches 16 total combinations.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16 combos
  - [wrong] 6 combos — Not quite. Six combos is the count for a pocket pair. A-K has 16 possible suit combinations before removing known cards.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16 combos
  + [correct] 16 combos — Nice count. A-K has 16 combos before blockers: 4 suited and 12 offsuit combinations. Blockers would remove visible or known cards from those private-card combinations.

TASK w6_pair_combos [drill] Pocket pair combo count
CAPTION: Pocket eights are one pair family.
Q: How many combos does 8-8 have?
HINT [theoryOnly]: You pick 2 suits out of the 4 eights in the deck.
TABLE: Preflop | You 8h 8c | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts pocket pair
SEATS: UTG 8h 8c stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
  + [correct] 6 combos — Nice count. Choose two of the four suits. That gives six possible pairs before removing known cards.
  - [wrong] 12 combos — Not quite. Twelve is too high for one pair family. With four eights in the deck, only 6 suit pairings are possible.
    BETTER ANSWER: 6 combos
  - [wrong] 16 combos — Not quite. Sixteen combos belongs to two different ranks like A-K, not to one pocket pair.
    BETTER ANSWER: 6 combos

TASK w6_combo_weight_compare [drill] Which family appears more?
CAPTION: Compare A-K with pocket eights before blockers.
Q: Which family has more possible combos?
HINT [theoryOnly]: One family has 16 combos. The other has 6.
TABLE: Preflop | You 7d 6d | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG 7d 6d stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
  - [wrong] They have the same combo count — Not quite. The hand names may feel equally important, but combo weight is not equal: 16 beats 6.
    BETTER ANSWER: A-K has more combos
  - [wrong] Pocket eights have more combos — Not quite. Pocket pairs have only 6 combos. Broad non-pair families like A-K are denser.
    BETTER ANSWER: A-K has more combos
  + [correct] A-K has more combos — Nice count. Before removing known cards, A-K has 16 combos and pocket eights have 6.

TASK w6_combo_counts_recap [review] Combo recap
CAPTION: Lesson learned: count the possible hands, then account for the action.
TEACH: Count before you guess. Count the available combos, then account for the action. Ten available combos count as five on average if each takes this action half the time.
TEACH LABELS: 16 combos, 6 combos, Range density
Q: What do combo counts help you measure?
HINT [theoryOnly]: A-K = 16 combos. A pocket pair = 6 combos.
TABLE: Preflop | You 9c 8c | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG 9c 8c stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
REVIEW: Combo counts tell you how many ways a hand can be dealt. The range also depends on how often each hand takes the action.

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON w6_continuation_bet · After your preflop raise =====

TASK w6_continuation_bet_intro [theory] The next bet after a raise
CAPTION: CO raised and BB called, then checked the flop. Read the three ranks and suits first. Ask which weaker hands could pay a small bet and which draws BB could continue with.
TEACH: Continuation bet, or c-bet A continuation bet is a flop bet by the player who last raised preflop. Against one caller who checks, a small bet is a good starting plan when you have a made hand on a dry flop. On a wet flop, check back if you missed and have no useful draw. The dry and wet textures tell you how many hands can connect, as in World 5. On a dry rainbow flop, a one-third-pot bet leaves weaker hands a smaller call. Connected two-tone flops give callers more ways to continue.
Q: How does the flop change your next decision?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Flop | You Ac Qd | Board Ah 6s 2c | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Ac Qd stack 97.25 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.25 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.75 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.75 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: CO can bet again after BB checks. A dry flop with a made hand gives weaker hands a reason to call a small bet.

TASK w6_continuation_bet_dry_size [drill] Size a bet on a dry flop
CAPTION: CO opened. BB called and checked on Q-7-2 rainbow. You have QJ.
Q: Which size fits the small-bet plan when weaker queens can call?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Flop | You Qc Jc | Board Qh 7s 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Qc Jc stack 97.25 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.25 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.75 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.75 BB more · Flop: BB checks
SIZES: 2 BB 0.3333333333333333 | 6 BB 1.0 | 9 BB 1.5
  + [correct] 2 BB — One third of the pot. In the 6 BB pot on Q-7-2 rainbow, a 2 BB bet with top pair gives weaker queens a manageable price.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Qc Jc | Board Qh 7s 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] 6 BB — That is a full-pot bet. On this dry flop, a 6 BB bet with QJ can drive out the weaker queens you want to call.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2 BB
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Qc Jc | Board Qh 7s 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] 9 BB — That is bigger than the pot. With QJ on Q-7-2, putting in 9 BB risks 7 BB more than the small bet and can leave you facing stronger hands.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2 BB
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Qc Jc | Board Qh 7s 2d | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

TASK w6_continuation_bet_value_size [drill] Bet a size that gets called
CAPTION: BB checked. In this example, weaker kings call bets of 3 BB or less.
Q: How much can you bet to get the most chips from those calls?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Flop | You Kh Qh | Board Kc 8d 3s | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Kh Qh stack 97.25 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97.25 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 2.75 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.75 BB more · Flop: BB checks
SIZES: 1.5 BB 0.25 | 6 BB 1.0 | 3 BB 0.5
  - [suboptimal] 1.5 BB — The bet leaves value behind. A weaker king calls 1.5 BB on K-8-3 in this example. If you pick that amount, you miss the extra 1.5 BB the same hand would pay.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 BB
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kh Qh | Board Kc 8d 3s | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] 6 BB — The weaker hands fold. The 6 BB bet is the size of the pot. BB folds weaker kings at that price in this example, costing you their 3 BB calls.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 BB
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kh Qh | Board Kc 8d 3s | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  + [correct] 3 BB — Three is the largest bet they call. KQ beats a weaker king on K-8-3. The half-pot size gets the full 3 BB those hands are willing to call.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kh Qh | Board Kc 8d 3s | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

TASK w6_continuation_bet_wet_check [review] Missed on a wet flop

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_reading_review · Review range reads and combinations =====

TASK range_checkpoint_combos [drill] Count a broadway hand
CAPTION: You have not seen an ace or a queen.
Q: How many A-Q combinations are possible?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Read the cards and the stated range.

  - [wrong] 12 — Count all suit combinations. Twelve counts only the offsuit hands. Four suited combinations are possible as well.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16
  - [wrong] 6 — A-Q has two different ranks. Six is the count for a pocket pair. For A-Q, any of four aces can go with any of four queens.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16
  + [correct] 16 — Four times four is sixteen. There are four aces and four queens available, giving 16 exact two-card hands.

===== WORLD 6 · LESSON range_thinking_checkpoint · Range thinking checkpoint =====

TASK w6_suited_offsuit_weight_compare [drill] Suited or offsuit weight
CAPTION: Compare A-K suited with A-K offsuit before blockers.
TEACH: Suited is rarer. Four aces can go with four kings. Four combinations match suits, leaving twelve offsuit combinations.
TEACH LABELS: 12 offsuit, 4 suited, Range weight
Q: How many combinations are suited and how many are offsuit?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Offsuit hands usually have more combinations than suited hands.
TABLE: Preflop | You Jh Th | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG Jh Th stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
  - [wrong] 12 suited, 4 offsuit — Easy trap. Suited feels special, but it is rarer. Only 4 suited combinations exist, while the offsuit family has 12.
    BETTER ANSWER: 4 suited, 12 offsuit
  + [correct] 4 suited, 12 offsuit — Clean weight read. A-K offsuit has 12 possible combos, while A-K suited has 4.
  - [wrong] 8 suited, 8 offsuit — Count the suited and offsuit combos. The rank names match, but combo weight does not. Twelve offsuit combos clearly outweigh four suited combos.
    BETTER ANSWER: 4 suited, 12 offsuit

TASK w6_pair_vs_suited_weight_compare [drill] Pair or suited family
CAPTION: Compare pocket nines with K-Q suited before blockers.
TEACH: Weight beats intuition. A pocket pair has six possible combos. A specified suited hand has four, one per suit.
TEACH LABELS: 6 pair combos, 4 suited combos, Use the count
Q: Which family has more possible combos?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Not every unpaired hand is denser than a pocket pair.
TABLE: Preflop | You Ac Jc | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Count combinations | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG Ac Jc stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
  - [wrong] K-Q suited — One more count. Unpaired does not always mean more common. Once you limit K-Q to suited only, it drops to 4 combos and loses to the pair family at 6.
    BETTER ANSWER: Pocket nines
  - [wrong] They have the same combo count — Count the pairs and suited combos. These families are closer than A-K versus a pocket pair, but they are still not equal. Six pair combos outweigh four suited combos.
    BETTER ANSWER: Pocket nines
  + [correct] Pocket nines — Good compare. Pocket nines have 6 possible combos, compared with 4 for K-Q suited.

  - [wrong] 9 AK offsuit, 9 pairs — Not quite. CO opens both families at the same frequency per combo, so twelve A-K offsuit combos carry twice the weight of six pocket-nine combos.
    BETTER ANSWER: 12 AK offsuit, 6 pairs

TASK w7_flop_bluff_one_player [drill] A flop decision
CAPTION: Compare what you win on folds with what you risk when someone continues.
Q: BB checks. Everyone folds to a 3 BB bet 40% of the time. For this exercise, count the full bet as lost if anyone continues. Checking has a value of 0 BB. Which action is better in this model?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Flop | You 7h 6h | Board As 9d 3c | Pot 6.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Center Flop decision | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO 7h 6h stack 97 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 97 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises to 3 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 2 BB more · Flop: BB checks
  + [correct] Bet 3 BB — That fits the table. With one opponent, the bet wins 6.5 BB on the 40% of hands where they fold and loses 3 BB otherwise. That is a gain of 0.8 BB on average in this example.
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You 7h 6h | Board As 9d 3c | Pot 6.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Flop decision | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight
  - [wrong] Check — Check what can still win. Checking gets 0 BB in this model. With BB as the only opponent, winning 6.5 BB on 40% of hands more than offsets the 3 BB you lose when BB continues.
    BETTER ANSWER: Bet 3 BB
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You 7h 6h | Board As 9d 3c | Pot 6.5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Flop decision | Facts high card, rainbow, backdoor straight

===== WORLD 8 · LESSON effective_stack_basics · Effective stack =====

TASK w7_effective_stack_intro [theory] Smaller stack rules
CAPTION: The smaller of two stacks caps what those players can match.
TEACH: Smaller stack rules. If you have 200 BB and the other player has 30 BB, the effective stack is 30 BB. That smaller stack sets the real risk.
TEACH LABELS: 200 BB, 30 BB, Effective stack
Q: What is the effective stack?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Compare the two players who can put chips in against each other.

TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises 2.5 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Between two players, the smaller stack caps what the two can still match.

===== WORLD 8 · LESSON same_hand_different_depth · Same hand, different depth =====

TASK w7_depth_shift_intro [theory] Depth changes the plan
CAPTION: Compare a short stack here with a deeper stack holding the same hand.
TEACH: Depth changes commitment. A short stack runs out sooner. It also limits how much you can win when a small pair makes a set or suited connectors make a strong hand. At 100 BB, you have more chips for bets on the same streets.
TEACH LABELS: 20 BB, 100 BB, More room, More risk
Q: Why does stack depth change the plan?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Short stacks simplify decisions. Deep stacks create more future risk.
TABLE: Flop | You As Js | Board Ac 7h 2c | Pot 5.5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Center Read the stack depth | Facts one pair, top pair, two-tone
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer As Js stack 20 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 20 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO folds · BTN raises 2.5 BB · SB folds · BB calls 1.5 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: The same hand can face bigger bets on the same streets when more chips are left.

===== WORLD 8 · LESSON spr_and_commitment · Room or commitment =====

TASK w7_spr_intro [theory] Low room vs high room
CAPTION: SPR tells you how much room is left after the flop.
TEACH: Divide the smaller stack by the pot. SPR is the stack-to-pot ratio: effective stack divided by the current pot. Here the smaller stack is 20 BB and the pot is 5 BB, so the SPR is 4.
TEACH LABELS: Low SPR, Commitment, High SPR, Room
Q: What does low SPR usually mean?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Low SPR means less money is left relative to the pot. Check your hand and the price before going all-in.
TABLE: Flop | You Ah Tc | Board Ac 8s 3d | Pot 5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Center Stack and pot | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO Ah Tc stack 20 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 100 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 35 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO raises 2.25 BB · BTN folds · SB folds · BB calls 1.25 BB more · Flop: BB checks
REVIEW: Compare the smaller remaining stack with the pot to see how much could still go in.

TASK w7_low_spr_commit [drill] SPR 2
CAPTION: SPR is 2 on the flop and you hold top pair.
Q: What does low SPR usually tell you?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Little room is left.

  - [wrong] Plenty of chips left for later bets — Not quite. The 10 BB left is only two times the 5 BB pot. Planning several large bets would use up those chips earlier than expected.
    BETTER ANSWER: One bet can commit the hand

    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kh 7d 3s | Pot 5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Stack and pot | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow
  - [wrong] It plays the same as SPR 8 — Not quite. A pot-sized 5 BB bet would put half of your 10 BB at risk. At SPR 8, it would risk only one eighth of the effective stack.
    BETTER ANSWER: One bet can commit the hand
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Kd Qc | Board Kh 7d 3s | Pot 5 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Center Stack and pot | Facts one pair, top pair, rainbow

===== WORLD 8 · LESSON format_pressure · 6-max vs full ring =====

TASK w7_format_intro [theory] Format changes pressure
CAPTION: This table is 6-max. At a nine-player full-ring table, UTG+1, UTG+2, and LJ also act after UTG.
TEACH: Fewer players behind. A full-ring table seats nine players. From UTG, eight players still act behind you, compared with five at a six-player table. With more players to act, open fewer hands.
TEACH LABELS: 6-max, Full ring, Fewer players behind
Q: Why does 6-max usually widen ranges?
HINT [theoryOnly]: Fewer players behind means less chance someone wakes up with a premium hand.
TABLE: Preflop | You Kd Jc | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat UTG | Active utg | Decision utg | Center Players behind | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG Kd Jc stack 100 BB | HJ stack 100 BB | CO stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB
REVIEW: From first position, a nine-handed table leaves more players to act than a six-handed table.

===== WORLD 9 · LESSON survival_pressure_basics · Chips and prizes =====

TASK w9_survival_intro [theory] Chips and prizes
CAPTION: Chips and expected prize money are different measures.
TEACH: Chips and prizes EV stands for expected value. It is your average result if you make the same choice many times. Chip EV counts chips. Prize EV counts prize money. Your run ends if you lose your stack. Near a payout, a small gain in chips can cost prize value. M = stack / (SB + BB + antes for one lap). Green is 20 or more. Yellow is 10 to under 20. Red is below 10.
Q: What does EV describe?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: EV includes winning and losing outcomes, weighted by their chances; one lost hand can come from a profitable decision.

TASK w9_cash_vs_tournament [drill] A close river call
CAPTION: Six left, five paid. Prizes in order: 500, 250, 120, 80, 50. BTN bets 16 BB into 8.5 BB and can bust you. The given range is 60% AQ or KQ and 40% missed JT. You win 40% with no ties. The prize model needs a 62.4% win rate.
TEACH: A close river call When a call can bust you, check both costs. First work out the chip price from the pot and call. Then compare your win rate with the prize model.
Q: Call or fold?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: River | You Qh Jh | Board Qs 9c 5d 2h 3s | Pot 24.5 BB | To call 16 BB | Seat BB | Active bb | Decision bb | Facts one pair, top pair
SEATS: UTG folded stack 2 BB | HJ folded stack 10 BB | CO folded stack 8 BB | BTN dealer stack 30 BB bet 16 BB | SB folded stack 9.5 BB | BB Qh Jh stack 16 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO folds · BTN raises to 2 BB · SB folds · BB calls 2 BB · Flop: BB checks · BTN bets 2 BB · BB calls 2 BB · Turn: BB checks · BTN checks · River: BB checks · BTN bets 16 BB
  + [correct] Fold — Correct. Keep 16 BB. Your 40% wins barely beat the chip price but fall below the 62.4% payout threshold while UTG has 2 BB.
  - [wrong] Call 16 BB — Look again. QJ beats the missed JT but loses to AQ/KQ. Calling earns 0.20 BB in chips yet drops modeled prize value from $192.16 to $123.25.
    BETTER ANSWER: Fold

TASK w9_ev_two_results [drill] Average chip gain
CAPTION: You gain 3 BB half the time. You lose 1 BB the other half.
Q: What is your chip EV?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] 1 BB — Correct. Half of 3 BB minus half of 1 BB leaves a gain of 1 BB.
  - [wrong] 2 BB — Look again. 3 BB minus 1 BB is the sum of both results. It is twice the gain per try.
    BETTER ANSWER: 1 BB
  - [wrong] 3 BB — Look again. 3 BB counts the wins. Skip the losses and the bet looks too good.
    BETTER ANSWER: 1 BB

TASK w9_short_stack_survival [drill] Small blind choice
CAPTION: You start with 9 BB. It folds to you in the small blind. The money is far off. BB calls an all-in with 77+, A9s+, ATo+ or KQs. BB folds the rest.
TEACH: Small blind choice An all-in puts your whole stack in. When just one player is left to act, an all-in can win the blinds. Check how often that player will call. This short-stack drill asks you to choose between an all-in and a fold.
Q: Go all-in or fold?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Kd 9d | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 0.5 BB | Seat SB | Active sb | Decision sb | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 28 BB | HJ folded stack 24 BB | CO folded stack 35 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 22 BB | SB Kd 9d stack 8.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 29 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO folds · BTN folds
  - [wrong] Fold — Look again. You start with 9 BB and face one tight caller. Folding K9s gives up the shot at the 1.5 BB pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: All-in to 9 BB
  + [correct] All-in to 9 BB — Correct. Add your remaining 8.5 BB. BB frequently folds under the stated calling-range model, letting K9s win the 1.5 BB pot before your stack shrinks.

TASK w9_survival_stack_tradeoff [drill] Price of busting
CAPTION: Two players have the same cards and chip price in two events.
Q: What shapes the cost of busting?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  - [wrong] Payouts without the other stacks — Look again. You have the prize ladder, but a 2 BB rival changes the cost of risking a medium stack; omitting that stack misses potential payout value.
    BETTER ANSWER: Payouts and the remaining stacks
  + [correct] Payouts and the remaining stacks — Correct. These describe what you can gain by advancing and how much prize value you risk by busting.
  - [wrong] Whether a reload is available — Look again. Reload availability does not supply the prize ladder or stack distribution; it cannot tell you whether a particular tournament call is profitable.
    BETTER ANSWER: Payouts and the remaining stacks

TASK w9_survival_recap [review] Chips and prizes recap
ENTRY: drill
CAPTION: Think back to the 20 BB call and the 9 BB all-in.
Q: Which plan balances growth and survival?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  - [suboptimal] Avoid thin calls but skip sound steals — Look again. Avoiding thin calls protects the stack, but passing the 9 BB SB opportunity also gives up chips available through folds.
    BETTER ANSWER: Take risks that improve prize EV
  - [wrong] Wait for AA before entering — Look again. The 9 BB K9s example already offered a sound first-in all-in; waiting for AA lets forced bets consume opportunities.
    BETTER ANSWER: Take risks that improve prize EV
  + [correct] Take risks that improve prize EV — Correct. That includes folding a costly bubble call and taking a sound first-in short-stack all-in.

===== WORLD 9 · LESSON m_ratio_zones_lite · M-ratio zones =====

TASK w9_m_ratio_intro [theory] How long will your stack last?
CAPTION: Sharky Three-Zone M
TEACH: How long will your stack last? M = stack / (SB + BB + antes for one lap). An ante is a forced fee. Green is 20 or more. Yellow is 10 to under 20. Red is below 10. At 0.5/1 with no ante, 12 BB gives M = 8.
Q: What does M estimate?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: Divide the starting stack by the blinds and orbit's antes; future blind rises and pots won or lost can change that estimate.

TASK w9_m_ratio_lap_count [drill] Laps left
CAPTION: Stack: 24 BB. Blinds: 0.5 and 1 BB. No antes.
Q: How many laps does M give you?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] 16 laps — Correct. Each lap costs 1.5 BB. Divide 24 by 1.5 to get 16.
  - [wrong] 24 laps — Look again. The big blind costs 1 BB. If you leave out the small blind, the stack seems to last too long.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16 laps
  - [wrong] 12 laps — Look again. The two blinds cost 1.5 BB, not 2 BB. Use the real cost or you may rush into a poor spot.
    BETTER ANSWER: 16 laps

===== WORLD 9 · LESSON bubble_risk_premium · Bubble risk premium =====

TASK w9_bubble_intro [theory] What does a call cost?
CAPTION: The money bubble is the last stage before those left win a prize.
TEACH: What does a call cost? Equity is your share of a pot on average. A tie gets its share too. Near a prize, a call that could bust you may need more equity than the chip price asks for. The gap is the risk premium. A stack that can bust yours covers you. Check the rest of the stacks and the prizes too.
Q: What is this example's risk premium?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: Subtract the chip threshold from the payout threshold: 55%-40%=15 percentage points.

TASK w9_bubble_premium_gap [drill] The extra cost of a call
CAPTION: You need to win 36% of the time for chips. The prize model needs 51%.
Q: How much extra equity does the call need?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  - [wrong] 36 points — Look again. 36% is the chip price. Using it as the gap overstates the extra cost.
    BETTER ANSWER: 15 points
  + [correct] 15 points — Correct. The gap from 36% to 51% is 15 points.
  - [wrong] 51 points — Look again. 51% is the whole target. Treating it as a gap counts the chip price twice.
    BETTER ANSWER: 15 points

  + [correct] Fold — Correct. Keep 16 BB instead of committing AQo against JJ+/AK while a 2 BB player remains below you.

===== WORLD 9 · LESSON tournament_pressure_checkpoint · Tournament pressure checkpoint =====

TASK w9_checkpoint_intro [theory] Read stack pressure
CAPTION: Five deals test how you read risk.
TEACH: Read stack pressure Read the hand and the action. Work out how long the stack can last. Check who can bust whom. When a prize model is given, use its inputs. The next five deals ask you to put these steps together.
Q: What belongs in the pressure read?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: Together these describe both the poker decision and the cost of tournament elimination.

TASK w9_prize_model_inputs [drill] What a prize model needs
CAPTION: One model gives a chip price. A second model gives the win rate you need to keep prize value.
Q: Which input belongs to the prize model?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  - [wrong] Your two card suits — Look again. Your suits can change your share of the pot. They give no value to the next paid place.
    BETTER ANSWER: The prize for each place
  - [wrong] The name of the street — Look again. The street tells you when the bet came. It does not tell you what you stand to win by moving up.
    BETTER ANSWER: The prize for each place
  + [correct] The prize for each place — Correct. A prize model needs the payouts and stacks. A bigger jump in prizes can change what a fold is worth.

===== WORLD 10 · LESSON player_type_basics · Who is at the table =====

TASK w10_player_type_intro [theory] How players act
CAPTION: Read how the table plays.
TEACH: How players act A nit plays few hands and folds a lot. A loose-passive player calls a lot and rarely raises. A calling station calls bets too much. An aggressive player bets and raises a lot. One who does so with too many weak hands is over-aggressive. An underbluffer bets strong hands and seldom bluffs. A 3-bet is a raise over an open raise. A c-bet is a flop bet by the player who raised preflop. These hands have no rake or antes.
Q: Which clue is most useful over time?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: Several hands can show how often a player folds, calls or bets. You can use that read in the next hand.

TASK w10_nit_tag [drill] Read both blinds
CAPTION: Both blinds are nits. They fold 90% of the time to either size. When one 3-bets, you fold.
TEACH: Read both blinds In the first-in chart, open Premium (AA–QQ and AKs) or Strong (JJ–TT, AKo, AQs and AJs) from UTG through BTN. Open Medium AQo, AJo, KQ and AT from HJ through BTN. Open Medium 99–22, KJ, QJs, KT and QT from CO or BTN. Fold Weak hands. This drill gives a rare exception based on who is left to act.
Q: Open or fold?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You 9s 7s | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 65 BB | HJ folded stack 70 BB | CO folded stack 62 BB | BTN dealer 9s 7s stack 45 BB | SB stack 47.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 49 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds · CO folds
  + [correct] Raise to 2 BB — Correct. The blinds fold 90% of the time. The steal earns 1.15 BB on average: 0.90 x 1.5 - 0.10 x 2.
  - [wrong] Fold — Look again. 97s is Weak in the base chart, but this strong read gives a 90% chance to win 1.5 BB without a flop. Folding misses that small steal.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 2 BB
  - [suboptimal] Raise to 4 BB — Look again. The same blinds fold 90% to either size in this read. A 4 BB open costs 2 BB more when one 3-bets.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 2 BB

TASK w10_loose_passive_tag [drill] Facing a limp
CAPTION: HJ limps for 1 BB. In 12 shown hands, HJ called with weak aces and small pairs. HJ rarely 3-bets.
TEACH: Facing a limp A limp is a call before the first raise. An isolation raise aims to play a pot with just the limper. Check the limper and seats behind you.
Q: How should you enter?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Ah Jd | Pot 2.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 70 BB | HJ stack 54 BB call 1 BB | CO Ah Jd stack 45 BB | BTN dealer stack 50 BB | SB stack 44.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 59 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ calls 1 BB
  - [suboptimal] Call 1 BB — Look again. AJo can play, but matching the 1 BB limp lets BTN and the blinds join for cheap. You miss value from HJ weak calls.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 4 BB
  + [correct] Raise to 4 BB — Correct. AJo is a Medium CO hand. The 4 BB raise puts more chips in against weak aces and pairs that HJ has called before.

===== WORLD 10 · LESSON adjust_one_lever · Adjust one piece =====

TASK w10_one_lever_intro [theory] Pick one change
CAPTION: One change at a time
TEACH: Pick one change A value bet aims to get a call from a worse hand. A bluff aims to make a better hand fold. Tie the size to your goal and what the player does. An overpair is a pair in your own cards that ranks above the top card on the board.
Q: A foe calls nine of ten bets. What is the risk?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: A pure bluff needs folds. Nine calls in ten bets leave few wins without showdown.

TASK w10_vs_nit_open_wider [drill] Three seats behind
CAPTION: BTN, SB and BB often fold to late opens. They fold as a group 88% of the time to 2 BB or 5 BB. When one 3-bets, you fold.
Q: Open or fold?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Js 9s | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat CO | Active co | Decision co | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 55 BB | HJ folded stack 65 BB | CO Js 9s stack 45 BB | BTN dealer stack 40 BB | SB stack 42.5 BB post 0.5 BB | BB stack 46 BB post 1 BB
TRAIL: SB blind 0.5 BB · BB blind 1 BB · UTG folds · HJ folds
  + [correct] Raise to 2 BB — Correct. The three players fold together 88%. Your small steal earns 1.08 BB on average under this read.
  - [wrong] Fold — Look again. J9s is Weak in the base CO chart. Still, folding here passes the 88% chance to take the 1.5 BB pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 2 BB
  - [suboptimal] Raise to 5 BB — Look again. This read gives the same folds to either size. Risking 5 BB instead of 2 BB gives up 3 BB more when someone 3-bets.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 2 BB

===== WORLD 10 · LESSON exploit_guardrails · Adjustment guardrails =====

TASK w10_guardrails_intro [theory] Check the read
CAPTION: A call has a price.
TEACH: Check the read A bluff-catcher beats bluffs. A blocker is a card you hold that rules out some hands. Divide the call by the pot after your call. Use the range and check the sample size.
Q: A river call is 5 into 10. What is its price?
HINT [theoryOnly]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REVIEW: Call 5 into a 10 BB pot now. Final pot 15 BB: 5/15 = 33.3%.

===== WORLD 10 · LESSON player_adjustment_checkpoint · Player-adjustment checkpoint =====

REVIEW: The pot sets the price. The bet range tells you how much of it your hand can beat.

  + [correct] 1 in 4 (25%) — Correct. 6 BB goes in a final pot of 24 BB. That is one in four.

    BETTER ANSWER: 1 in 4 (25%)

===== WORLD 11 · LESSON session_plan_basics · Session plan in 30 seconds =====

TASK w11_session_plan_intro [theory] One-focus plan
CAPTION: A short plan helps you spot one leak while you play.
TEACH: One-focus plan Choose a cue you can see during play. Use it to test a past leak. Bankroll means funds set aside for poker, not rent or other needs. These cash-game drills have no rake or antes.
Q: Which plan can you track?
HINT [hidden]: (none)

  - [wrong] Six skills to track at once — Look again. Six live cues split your focus. You may miss the one BB choice that you meant to study.
    BETTER ANSWER: One clear skill to watch
  - [wrong] A win goal for the day — Look again. A cash win can depend on luck. It does not show whether you read the next bet well.
    BETTER ANSWER: One clear skill to watch

TASK w11_bankroll_rule [drill] Bankroll rule
CAPTION: Sharky cash-game plan: keep 40 full buy-ins for your stake. NL25 is $0.10/$0.25.
TEACH: Bankroll rule A full buy-in is 100 BB. Our course uses a buffer of 40 full buy-ins for cash games. At NL10, a full buy-in is $10. At NL5, it is $5. This is a risk guide, not a promise of profit.

    BETTER ANSWER: $1,000
  - [wrong] $100 — Look again. $100 covers four $25 buy-ins. A few losses could use the funds set aside for play.
    BETTER ANSWER: $1,000
  + [correct] $1,000 — Correct. At NL25 the big blind is $0.25. A full buy-in is $25. Forty buy-ins need $1,000.

===== WORLD 11 · LESSON table_trigger_reads · In-session trigger reads =====

TASK w11_trigger_intro [theory] Trigger-first routine
CAPTION: Read the table, then pick one response.
TEACH: Trigger-first routine A multiway pot has three or more players on the flop. A c-bet is a flop bet by the preflop raiser. A 3-bet is a raise over an open raise. SPR is the smaller stack left after preflop, divided by the flop pot. An overpair is a pocket pair above the top board card. Check cards, seat, price and the player read.
Q: Flop pot 6, stack left 12: what SPR?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG | HJ | CO | BTN dealer | SB | BB
  + [correct] 2 — Correct. SPR is 12/6=2. You have twice the pot left to play.
  - [wrong] 6 — Look again. 6 BB is the pot size, not the ratio. The 12 BB stack is twice that pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2
  - [wrong] 12 — Look again. 12 BB is the stack left, not the ratio. Divide it by the 6 BB pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2

TASK w11_trigger_overfold_blinds [drill] Blind overfold trigger

  - [wrong] Fold — Look again. A7o is weak in the base chart, but the observed 88% BB folds make a small SB steal worth more than giving up the blind.
    BETTER ANSWER: Raise to 2 BB
  + [correct] Raise to 2 BB — Correct. BB folds 88%. From this decision, the 2 BB open gains 1.14 BB on average: 0.88 x 1.5 - 0.12 x 1.5. SB has already put in 0.5 BB. The base chart is a guide for first-in hands. A tested player read can change a close choice. Check risk and the fold rate.

TASK w11_trigger_bad_price_fold [drill] A tight turn raise
CAPTION: CO bets 8 into 10 on K-8-4-2. In eight past big turn bets, CO showed sets, K8 or AK in seven. Assume KQ wins 15% against this betting range by the river, about 1 in 7.
Q: Call or fold?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Turn | You Kc Qd | Board Ks 8d 4c 2h | Pot 18 BB | To call 8 BB | Seat SB | Active sb | Decision sb | Facts one pair, top pair
SEATS: UTG folded stack 65 BB | HJ folded stack 62 BB | CO stack 46.5 BB bet 8 BB | BTN folded dealer stack 57 BB | SB Kc Qd stack 32.5 BB | BB folded stack 49 BB

===== WORLD 11 · LESSON post_session_review_loop · Post-session review habit =====

TEACH: Pick priority leak The next focus should come from what the record shows. Count repeated errors, then name the same clue you missed. Do not call a lucky win a fixed leak.

HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts

  - [wrong] The largest pot you won — Look again. A large win is not listed as an error. It gives no reason to skip the four bad BB calls.
    BETTER ANSWER: BB call price against strong bets
  + [correct] BB call price against strong bets — Correct. Four BB price errors give more repeated evidence than the one missed value bet.

TASK w11_review_define_fix [drill] Define tomorrow fix

HINT [hidden]: (none)

  + [correct] On a turn raise, check range and call price — Correct. The cue names the turn raise and two facts to test before putting more chips in.

    BETTER ANSWER: On a turn raise, check range and call price
  - [wrong] Win back the cost of the error — Look again. The money lost is gone. A chase goal can cause another poor call in a new pot.

===== WORLD 11 · LESSON real_play_transfer_checkpoint · Real-play session checkpoint =====

TASK w11_checkpoint_intro [drill] Session cycle map
CAPTION: Five new hands test the full live table read.
TEACH: Session cycle map Read the seat, cards and board. A pot price is the call divided by the final pot. Check each player who may still act. After you choose, review the reason.
Q: An example pot starts with 8 BB. Your call would match a 4 BB wager. What is the call price?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG | HJ | CO | BTN dealer | SB | BB
  + [correct] 25% — Correct. The pot has 12 after the bet. Calling 4 makes 16. The price is 4/16=25%.
  - [wrong] 33.3% — Look again. 4/12 leaves out your own call. The final pot is 16, so the call price is lower.
    BETTER ANSWER: 25%
  - [wrong] 50% — Look again. The 4 BB bet is half of the old 8 BB pot. The call cost uses the 16 BB final pot.
    BETTER ANSWER: 25%

===== WORLD 12 · LESSON decision_over_outcome · Decision quality over outcome =====

TASK w12_decision_quality_intro [theory] Process first
CAPTION: A good choice can lose. A poor choice can win.
TEACH: Process first EV means expected value: the average gain or loss over many repeats. An out is a card that makes a losing hand win. On the turn, count clean outs, not cards that help the other player more. A river call needs a win rate high enough for its price. A c-bet is a flop bet from the preflop raiser.
Q: What should you test after a lucky win?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG | HJ | CO | BTN dealer | SB | BB
  + [correct] The price and range you faced — Correct. A lucky river can hide a bad call. The old price and the likely hands decide if it had value.
  - [wrong] The size of the pot you won — Look again. A large pot can come from a weak call. Pot size alone does not show if the price was good.
    BETTER ANSWER: The price and range you faced
  - [wrong] How happy the win made you — Look again. A good feeling is real, but it does not show if your hand had enough wins for the bet.
    BETTER ANSWER: The price and range you faced

TASK w12_good_fold_bad_result [drill] A new river decision

TEACH: A new river decision One shown card can help you learn. It does not replace a larger group of showdowns. On the river, there is no next card to save a weak call.

TEACH: River price W5’s clean outs matter while another card can come. On the river the board is complete. A bluff-catcher beats bluffs but loses to value hands. Use W4’s call price: divide the call by the pot after the bet and your call. Compare that price with the share of bluffs.

===== WORLD 12 · LESSON tilt_reset_protocol · Tilt reset protocol =====

TASK w12_tilt_reset_intro [theory] Reset in under 20s
CAPTION: What happened in the last hand can affect your next choice.
TEACH: Reset in under 20s Tilt is when anger, fear or stress starts to steer your play. A quick reset can protect the next hand. You can note the feeling, slow your next choice and check the table facts. If focus does not return, you can leave the session. A pause does not change pot odds.
Q: What can a reset protect?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG | HJ | CO | BTN dealer | SB | BB
  + [correct] The next choice from the last hand's mood — Correct. The prior loss is over. A reset helps you read new cards and stakes without trying to get even.

===== WORLD 12 · LESSON confidence_and_discipline · Confidence with discipline =====

TASK w12_confidence_intro [theory] Calm assertive posture
CAPTION: A river example starts with 16 BB in the middle. A rival adds 8 BB, making the pot 24 BB.
TEACH: Calm assertive posture Confidence does not mean a larger bet. Start by reading the chips already in the pot. Your own chips enter only if you call. An overpair is a pocket pair above the top board card. A bluff-catcher beats bluffs but loses to value hands. Call price equals the call divided by the pot after your call.
Q: What is the call price?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Seat CO | Center Hypothetical example | Empty board Use the stated premise | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG | HJ | CO | BTN dealer | SB | BB
  + [correct] 25% — Correct. The pot now has 24 BB. Calling 8 makes 32 BB. Your price is 8/32 = 25%.
  - [wrong] 33.3% — Look again. A call would make the 24 BB pot grow to 32 BB. Dividing by 24 leaves out your own call.
    BETTER ANSWER: 25%
  - [wrong] 50% — Look again. Calling 8 BB can win more than 8. The final pot is 32 BB, so 50% is far too high.
    BETTER ANSWER: 25%

===== WORLD 1 · LESSON what_poker_is · First Table Guide =====

  + [correct] Bet earns 1.2 BB on average — Correct. A fold wins the 6 BB pot, worth 2.4 BB on average. Calls lose 2 BB, costing 1.2 BB on average. The difference is positive 1.2 BB.

    BETTER ANSWER: Bet earns 1.2 BB on average
    FEEDBACK TABLE: Flop | You Jh 9s | Board As 6c 2s | Pot 6 BB | Seat CO | Card focus board_0, board_1, board_2 | Facts high card, two-tone, backdoor flush
